FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by Shearing and Allied Equipments Fasteners for Consumer Goods and Hair Cutting, Shaving, Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. The razor blade industry has been feeling the need for a national standard covering the requirements for razor handles due to its increasing demand in the domestic market and popularity These shaving systems are also being among the consumers in view of safety and smooth shaving. exported in large numbers and the standard would help those exporting and intending to export these types of shaving systems. For the purpose of-deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing a result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

6.1 Twin blade razor handle shall fit into the accommoda?e twin blade cartridges conforming to IS 13031 : 1990. When assembled with the cartridge this should be evenly balanced. Cartridge alignment pattern shall be with sliding type or swivel type. The handle shall be knurled, grooved or serrated to provide a firm grip when used in a manner consistent with normal use. The length of the handle and the area of crosssection shall be of minimum 100 mm and 30 mm2 respectively measured on the largest cross-section. The razor design shall provide proper positioning of cartridges for satisfactory shaving. 6.2 Twin blade razor handle shall provide secure fit and shall not loosen while shaving. 6.3 Razor operate. handle shall be durable a

6.4 Cartridge changing in sliding type is by sliding the razor slide at the back of the cartridge and in swivel type by inserting the razor finger at the groove provided at the back of the cartridges. 6.5 All components of the razor handle shall be grooved or smoothly finished and serrated, knurled. Surfaces shall be free from sharp edges or burrs. The slider shall be perpendicular to the handle axis. 7 FINISH 7.1 The components of safety razors made of non-ferrous metal, except aluminium, shall be plated chromium over nickel having a thickness of nickel plating of minimum 20 microns. For nickel plating shall other requirements the conform to Service Grade No. 3 of IS 1068 : 1993. The aluminium components shall be anodized in accordance with Grade AC5 of IS 1868 : 1982. 8 TEST

Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity Details of conditions under which a licence for the to that standard as a further safeguard. use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
